description: The plot illustrates how loss changes as a function of compute (TFLOPs) for two methods, shown as two lines. The x-axis is labeled “TFLOPs,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately 0.00 to 1.25 with an offset notation of 1e9 (i.e., values are in billions of TFLOPs); tick labels appear at regular 0.25 intervals (0.00, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00, 1.25). The y-axis is labeled “Loss,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from about 2.40 to 2.75 with evenly spaced ticks every 0.05. One line labeled “Vanilla” is purple with upward-pointing triangle markers connected by a solid line; it starts near the top-left around loss ≈2.75 at very low TFLOPs, decreases steadily, and ends near loss ≈2.50 at about 1.2×10^9 TFLOPs. The second line is red with circular markers connected by a solid line; it begins around loss ≈2.74 at very low TFLOPs, drops to about 2.60 by roughly 0.2×10^9 TFLOPs, continues decreasing through about 2.50 near ~0.9×10^9 TFLOPs, and finishes around 2.47–2.48 at about 1.2×10^9 TFLOPs. Green dashed guide lines annotate a horizontal level at loss = 2.50 and a vertical region near the right side, with a green dashed bracket labeled “1.28×” spanning a portion of the high-TFLOPs range.
